title.en: 新唐書卷七十四 表第十四上 宰相世系四上

translations.literal: The Wei clan traces its origin to the Feng surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei clan descended from the Feng lineage.

sentences.zh: 顓頊孫大彭為夏諸侯，少康之世，封其別孫元哲于豕韋，其地滑州韋城是也。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu's descendant Da Peng was a feudal lord of Xia; in the era of Shaokang, his collateral descendant Yuan Zhe was enfeoffed at Zhuxiang Wei, which is the Wei walled city in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Da Peng, a descendant of Zhuanxu, served as a Xia feudatory lord; during the reign of Shaokang, a collateral descendant named Yuan Zhe was granted Zhuxiang Wei—present-day Wei City in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 豕韋、大彭迭為商伯，周赧王時，始失國，徙居彭城，以國為氏。

translations.literal: Zhuxiang Wei and Da Peng alternated as overlords of Shang; in the time of King Nan of Zhou they first lost their state, moved to reside at Pengcheng, and took the state name as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuxiang Wei and Da Peng took turns as Shang overlords; under King Nan of Zhou the line finally lost its state, resettled at Pengcheng, and adopted the former realm as their surname.

sentences.zh: 韋伯遐二十四世孫孟，為漢楚王傅，去位，徙居魯國鄒縣。

translations.literal: Meng, the twenty-fourth-generation descendant of Earl Wei Xia, served as tutor to the King of Chu in Han, left office, and moved to reside in Zou County in the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, twenty-four generations removed from Earl Wei Xia, had been tutor to the Han Prince of Chu; he resigned his post and settled in Zou County in Lu.

sentences.zh: 孟四世孫賢，漢丞相、扶陽節侯，又徙京兆杜陵。

translations.literal: Xian, Meng's descendant in the fourth generation, was Han chancellor and Marquis Jie of Fuyang, and again moved to Dulang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, four generations after Meng, rose to Han chancellor and Marquis Jie of Fuyang, and the family moved once more to Dulang in the Jingzhao commandery.

translations.literal: He fathered Xuancheng, chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Xuancheng, who also became chancellor.

translations.literal: He fathered Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng's son was Kuan.

translations.literal: Kuan fathered Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan had a son named Yu.

translations.literal: Yu fathered Jun, Later Han Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was followed by Jun, who served as Director of the Masters of Writing under the Later Han.

translations.literal: He fathered Bao, Administrator of Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Bao became Administrator of Zitong.

translations.literal: He fathered Zhuo, Chancellor of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was succeeded by Zhuo, who served as Chancellor of Donghai.

translations.literal: His grandson Zhou was Wei Household Mentor and Marquis of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's grandson Zhou held the posts of Household Mentor in Wei and Marquis of Ancheng.

translations.literal: Three sons: Qian, Mu, and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Qian, Mu, and Yin.

translations.literal: Qian was styled "Western Branch," Mu was styled "Eastern Branch."
translations.idiomatic: Qian's line was called the Western Branch; Mu's line was called the Eastern Branch.

sentences.zh: 潛曾孫惠度，後魏中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Huidu, Qian's great-grandson, was Later Wei Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's great-grandson Huidu served as Vice Director of the Secretariat under the Later Wei.

translations.literal: He fathered Qianxiong, Administrator of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu was followed by Qianxiong, Administrator of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 生鄭子，字英，代郡守、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He fathered Zhengzi, styled Ying, Administrator of Dai Commandery and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiong's son Zhengzi, courtesy name Ying, became Administrator of Dai and Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 生瑱，字世珍，後周侍中、平齊惠公，號平齊公房。

translations.literal: He fathered Zhen, styled Shizhen, Later Zhou Palace Attendant and Duke Hui of Pingqi, styled the Pingqi Duke Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzi's son Zhen, courtesy name Shizhen, rose to Palace Attendant under the Later Zhou and was ennobled as Duke Hui of Pingqi; his descendants formed the Pingqi Duke Branch.

translations.literal: Two sons: Jun and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Jun and Shi.

sentences.zh: 東眷韋氏：穆曾孫楷，晉長樂、清河二郡守。

translations.literal: Eastern Branch Wei clan: Kai, Mu's great-grandson, was Administrator of both Changle and Qinghe commanderies in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Branch of the Wei clan: Kai, Mu's great-grandson, held the governorships of Changle and Qinghe under the Jin.

translations.literal: He fathered Kui, Murong Chui's Grand Chamberlain for the Palace Harem.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's son Kui served Murong Chui as Grand Chamberlain for the Palace Harem.

sentences.zh: 生閬，字友觀，避地薊城，後魏太武召為咸陽太守。

translations.literal: He fathered Lang, styled Youguan, who took refuge in Jicheng; Later Wei Emperor Taiwu summoned him as Administrator of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's son Lang, courtesy name Youguan, fled to Jicheng for safety; Emperor Taiwu of the Later Wei later appointed him Administrator of Xianyang.

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong was in great disorder, but the territory under his administration alone remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: While the Guanzhong region was torn by widespread disorder, the district under his rule alone stayed at peace.

sentences.zh: 明元帝嘗曰：「我欲有臣皆如閬。」

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan once said: "I wish all my ministers were like Lang."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan once remarked, "I wish every minister I had were like Lang."

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as a fine anecdote.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries took the remark as a celebrated compliment.

translations.literal: His descendants therefore separately styled themselves the Lang Duke Branch.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants accordingly formed a separate line known as the Lang Duke Branch.

translations.literal: Two sons: Fan and Daozhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Fan and Daozhen.

sentences.zh: 道珍字秦寶，後魏威遠將軍、扶風馮翊二郡太守。

translations.literal: Daozhen, styled Qinbao, was Later Wei General Who Establishes Might in the Distance and Administrator of both Fufeng and Fengyi commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhen, courtesy name Qinbao, served the Later Wei as General Who Establishes Might in the Distance and as Administrator of Fufeng and Fengyi.

translations.literal: He fathered Yong, Gentleman of the Palace Library and Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhen's son Yong held the posts of Gentleman of the Palace Library and Grand Master of Remonstrance.

translations.literal: He fathered Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was succeeded by Hongzhou.

translations.literal: Two sons: Cheng and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Cheng and Yan.

sentences.zh: 淹生雲起，封彭城公，因號彭城公房。

translations.literal: Yan fathered Yunqi, who was enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng, and therefore was styled the Pengcheng Duke Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Yunqi was ennobled as Duke of Pengcheng, and his line became known as the Pengcheng Duke Branch.

sentences.zh: 逍遙公房出自閬弟子真嘉，後魏侍中、馮翊扶風二郡守。

translations.literal: The Carefree Duke Branch issued from Lang's younger brother Zhenjia, Later Wei Palace Attendant and Administrator of both Fengyi and Fufeng commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Carefree Duke Branch descended from Lang's younger brother Zhenjia, who served the Later Wei as Palace Attendant and as Administrator of Fengyi and Fufeng.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xu and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xu and Zhi.

translations.literal: Xu was Inspector of Southern Youzhou and Duke Hui of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Xu became Inspector of Southern Youzhou and was ennobled as Duke Hui of Wen.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xiong and Shuyu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xiong and Shuyu.

sentences.zh: 敻字敬遠，後周逍遙公，號逍遙公房。

translations.literal: Xiong, styled Jingyuan, was Later Zhou Duke of Carefree Leisure, styled the Carefree Duke Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, courtesy name Jingyuan, was made Duke of Carefree Leisure under the Later Zhou, and his line took the name Carefree Duke Branch.

sentences.zh: 八子：世康、洸、瓘、頤、仁基、藝、沖、約。

translations.literal: Eight sons: Shikang, Guang, Guan, Yi, Renji, Yi, Chong, and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons: Shikang, Guang, Guan, Yi, Renji, Yi, Chong, and Yue.

sentences.zh: 鄖公房：文惠公旭次子叔裕，字孝寬，隋尚書令、鄖襄公。

translations.literal: Yun Duke Branch: Shuyu, Duke Hui of Wen's second son Xu, styled Xiaokuan, was Sui Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke Xiang of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The Yun Duke Branch: Shuyu, the second son of Duke Hui of Wen (Xu), courtesy name Xiaokuan, rose to Sui Director of the Masters of Writing and was ennobled as Duke Xiang of Yun.

sentences.zh: 六子：諶、總、壽、霽、津、靜，號鄖公房。

translations.literal: Six sons: Chen, Zong, Shou, Ji, Jin, and Jing, styled the Yun Duke Branch.
translations.idiomatic: His six sons—Chen, Zong, Shou, Ji, Jin, and Jing—formed what was called the Yun Duke Branch.

sentences.zh: 南皮公房：安城侯胄次子愔。

translations.literal: Nanpi Duke Branch: Yin, Marquis of Ancheng Zhou's second son.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanpi Duke Branch: descended from Yin, the second son of Marquis of Ancheng Zhou.

sentences.zh: 愔七代孫景略，後周驃騎將軍、右光祿大夫、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Jinglue, Yin's descendant in the seventh generation, was Later Zhou General of Agile Cavalry, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after Yin came Jinglue, who served the Later Zhou as General of Agile Cavalry, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 生瓚，隋倉部侍郎、尚書右丞、司農卿、南皮縣伯。

translations.literal: He fathered Zan, Sui Vice Minister of the Revenue Section, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Minister of Finance for the Imperial Households, and Baron of Nanpi County.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglue's son Zan held Sui posts as Vice Minister of the Revenue Section, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Minister of Finance for the Imperial Households, and was ennobled as Baron of Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 四子：叔諧、季武、叔謙、季貞，因號南皮公房。

translations.literal: Four sons: Shuxie, Jiwu, Shuqian, and Jizhen, and therefore styled the Nanpi Duke Branch.
translations.idiomatic: His four sons—Shuxie, Jiwu, Shuqian, and Jizhen—gave the line its name as the Nanpi Duke Branch.

sentences.zh: 瓚從子元遜，從祖弟子述。

translations.literal: Zan's younger cousin's son Yuanyun, and his father's younger brother's son's son Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Among Zan's kin were his younger cousin's son Yuanyun and his father's younger brother's grandson Shu.

sentences.zh: 駙馬房：東眷穆四代孫自璧，自璧四代孫延賓，延賓三子：璋、福、議。

translations.literal: Imperial Son-in-Law Branch: Zibi, Eastern Branch Mu's descendant in the fourth generation; Yanbin, Zibi's descendant in the fourth generation; Yanbin's three sons: Zhang, Fu, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Son-in-Law Branch: Zibi, four generations from Eastern Branch Mu; Yanbin, four generations from Zibi; and Yanbin's three sons Zhang, Fu, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 至溫，諸子尚主者數人，因號駙馬房。

translations.literal: Down to Wen, several sons married imperial princesses, and therefore it was styled the Imperial Son-in-Law Branch.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Wen, several men of the line had married imperial princesses, and the branch accordingly came to be called the Imperial Son-in-Law Branch.

sentences.zh: 龍門公房：安城侯胄次子愔，愔生達，達六世孫挺傑，後周撫軍將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: Longmen Duke Branch: Yin, Marquis of Ancheng Zhou's second son; Yin fathered Da; Tingjie, Da's descendant in the sixth generation, was Later Zhou General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Longmen Duke Branch: from Yin, Zhou's second son; through Da, six generations down to Tingjie, who served the Later Zhou as General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Pingzhou.

translations.literal: Two sons: Zun and Tong.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zun and Tong.

sentences.zh: 遵，驃騎大將軍、晉州大總管府長史、龍門縣公，因號龍門公房。

translations.literal: Zun was General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Chief Clerk of the Grand Commander's Office of Jinzhou, and Duke of Longmen County, and therefore was styled the Longmen Duke Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Zun rose to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Chief Clerk of the Jinzhou Grand Commander's Office, was ennobled as Duke of Longmen County, and gave his name to the Longmen Duke Branch.

translations.literal: Tong fathered Shansi.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was succeeded by Shansi.

sentences.zh: 小逍遙公房出自東眷穆孫鍾。

translations.literal: The Lesser Carefree Duke Branch issued from Eastern Branch Mu's grandson Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Carefree Duke Branch descended from Zhong, grandson of Eastern Branch Mu.

sentences.zh: 鍾生華，隨宋高祖度江居襄陽，生玄，以太尉掾召，不赴。

translations.literal: Zhong fathered Hua, who with Song Gaozu crossed the Yangzi and settled in Xiangyang; Hua fathered Xuan, who was summoned as a clerk in the Grand Marshal's office but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's son Hua followed Song Gaozu across the Yangzi and settled in Xiangyang; Hua's son Xuan was summoned to serve as a clerk under the Grand Marshal but declined the appointment.

translations.literal: Two sons: Zuzheng, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zuzheng, who became Grand Master for Splendid Happiness;

translations.literal: Zugui, Chief Clerk of Pacifying the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: and Zugui, who served as Chief Clerk of Pacifying the Distance.

translations.literal: Zugui's three sons: Zuan, Chan, and Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Zugui had three sons: Zuan, Chan, and Rui.

translations.literal: Zuan was Southern Qi Registrar in the Office of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan served the Southern Qi as Registrar in the Office of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 曾孫弘瑗，至嗣立更號小逍遙公房。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Hongyuan; down to Sili the name was changed again to the Lesser Carefree Duke Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's great-grandson was Hongyuan; by the time of Sili the line was restyled the Lesser Carefree Duke Branch.

translations.literal: There was also the Jingzhao Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a separate Jingzhao branch of the Wei clan.

translations.literal: There was also the Jingzhao Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: There was likewise the Jingzhao Wei line.

sentences.zh: 韋氏定著九房：一曰西眷，二曰東眷，三曰逍遙公房，四曰鄖公房，五曰南皮公房，六曰駙馬房，七曰龍門公房，八曰小逍遙公房，九曰京兆韋氏。

translations.literal: The Wei clan was definitively recorded as nine branches: first the Western Branch, second the Eastern Branch, third the Carefree Duke Branch, fourth the Yun Duke Branch, fifth the Nanpi Duke Branch, sixth the Imperial Son-in-Law Branch, seventh the Longmen Duke Branch, eighth the Lesser Carefree Duke Branch, ninth the Jingzhao Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei clan was formally divided into nine recognized branches: the Western Branch, the Eastern Branch, the Carefree Duke Branch, the Yun Duke Branch, the Nanpi Duke Branch, the Imperial Son-in-Law Branch, the Longmen Duke Branch, the Lesser Carefree Duke Branch, and the Jingzhao Wei line.

translations.literal: Fourteen chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen men of the clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: The Pingqi Duke Branch had Baoheng and Hongmin;
translations.idiomatic: From the Pingqi Duke Branch came Baoheng and Hongmin;

translations.literal: the Eastern Branch had Fangzhi;
translations.idiomatic: the Eastern Branch produced Fangzhi;

sentences.zh: 逍遙公房有貫之、處厚、待價；

translations.literal: the Carefree Duke Branch had Guanzhi, Chuhou, and Daijia;
translations.idiomatic: the Carefree Duke Branch yielded Guanzhi, Chuhou, and Daijia;

translations.literal: the Yun Duke Branch had Juyuan;
translations.idiomatic: the Yun Duke Branch had Juyuan;

translations.literal: the Nanpi Duke Branch had Jiansu;
translations.idiomatic: the Nanpi Duke Branch produced Jiansu;

translations.literal: the Imperial Son-in-Law Branch had Wen;
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Son-in-Law Branch had Wen;

translations.literal: the Longmen Duke Branch had Zhiyi;
translations.idiomatic: the Longmen Duke Branch produced Zhiyi;

translations.literal: Xiangyang had Siqian and Sili;
translations.idiomatic: the Xiangyang line contributed Siqian and Sili;

translations.literal: Jingzhao had Yifan and Zhaodu.
translations.idiomatic: and Jingzhao had Yifan and Zhaodu.

translations.literal: The Guo clan traces its origin to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Guo clan descended from the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 周武王封文王弟虢叔於西虢，封虢仲於東虢。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed King Wen's younger brother Uncle Guo in Western Guo and enfeoffed Uncle Zhong Guo in Eastern Guo.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou granted Western Guo to King Wen's younger brother Uncle Guo and Eastern Guo to Uncle Zhong Guo.

sentences.zh: 西虢地在虞、鄭之間，平王東遷，奪虢叔之地與鄭武公，楚莊王起陸渾之師伐周，責王滅虢，於是平王求虢叔裔孫序，封於陽曲，號曰郭公。

translations.literal: Western Guo lay between Yu and Zheng; when King Ping moved east, he seized Uncle Guo's territory and gave it to Duke Wu of Zheng; King Zhuang of Chu raised the army of Luhun to attack Zhou and reproached the king for destroying Guo; thereupon King Ping sought Uncle Guo's collateral descendant Xu, enfeoffed him at Yangqu, and styled him Duke Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Western Guo lay between Yu and Zheng; when King Ping moved the capital eastward he stripped Uncle Guo's domain and gave it to Duke Wu of Zheng; later King Zhuang of Chu marched the army of Luhun against Zhou and charged the Zhou king with extinguishing Guo; King Ping then found Uncle Guo's collateral descendant Xu, enfeoffed him at Yangqu, and styled him Duke Guo.

sentences.zh: 「虢」謂之「郭」，聲之轉也，因以為氏。

translations.literal: "Guo" was called "Guo" [homophone written differently]—a shift in sound—and they therefore took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The name for the state of Guo was pronounced and written as the homophone Guo meaning 'outer moat' through a regular sound change, and the clan adopted the latter form as its surname.

sentences.zh: 後漢末，大司農郭全代居陽曲，生蘊。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Han, Grand Minister of Agriculture Guo Quan of Dai resided at Yangqu and fathered Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Later Han, Grand Minister of Agriculture Guo Quan of Dai lived at Yangqu and had a son named Yun.

translations.literal: Yun fathered Zhun, Pei, and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had three sons: Zhun, Pei, and Zhen.

translations.literal: Zhen was Master of Ceremonies and Marquis of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen served as Master of Ceremonies and was ennobled as Marquis of Changping.

translations.literal: A descendant moved to Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: A later descendant of the line resettled in Yingchuan.

translations.literal: The Huayin Guo clan also issued from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayin branch of the Guo clan likewise traced its origin to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 漢有郭亭，亭曾孫光祿大夫廣智，廣智生馮翊太守孟儒，子孫自太原徙馮翊。

translations.literal: In Han there was Guo Ting; Ting's great-grandson Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Guangzhi; Guangzhi fathered Administrator of Fengyi Mengru, and descendants moved from Taiyuan to Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han there was Guo Ting; four generations later came Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Guangzhi; Guangzhi's son Mengru became Administrator of Fengyi, and the family moved from Taiyuan to Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 後魏有同州司馬徽，徽弟進。

translations.literal: In Later Wei there was Tongzhou Militia Commander Hui, and Hui's younger brother Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Wei the line included Tongzhou Militia Commander Hui and his younger brother Jin.

translations.literal: The Changle Guo clan also issued from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Changle branch of the Guo clan also came out of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 後漢郭泰，字林宗，世居介休，司徒黃瓊辟太常，趙典舉有道，皆不應，世稱為郭有道。

translations.literal: Later Han's Guo Tai, styled Linzong, dwelt for generations at Jiexiu; Minister of Education Huang Qiong summoned him to the Grand Master of Ceremonies, Zhao Dian recommended him as Cultivated Talent, and he responded to none of them; his age called him Master Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Han, Guo Tai, courtesy name Linzong, had long lived at Jiexiu; Minister of Education Huang Qiong invited him to the post of Grand Master of Ceremonies and Zhao Dian nominated him as a Cultivated Talent candidate, but he accepted neither summons; contemporaries honored him as Master Guo.

translations.literal: A descendant resided at Changle in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of his line settled at Changle in Weizhou.

translations.literal: In Tang there was Inspector of Jizhou Shan'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang the line produced Shan'ai, Inspector of Jizhou.

translations.literal: The Zhongshan Guo clan dwelt for generations at Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongshan branch of the Guo clan had long resided at Gucheng.

translations.literal: In Tang there was Zhengyi, who served as chancellor to Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, Zhengyi served as chancellor to Emperor Gaozong.

translations.literal: He fathered Zhong, Master of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Zhong, who became Master of Communications.

translations.literal: The Guo clan had four chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Four men of the Guo clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Daiju, Ziyi, Yuanzhen, and Zhengyi.
translations.idiomatic: They were Daiju, Ziyi, Yuanzhen, and Zhengyi.

translations.literal: The Wu clan traces its origin to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu clan descended from the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 周平王少子生而有文在手曰「武」，遂以為氏。

translations.literal: King Ping of Zhou's youngest son was born with writing on his hand reading "Wu," and they therefore took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: A youngest son of King Ping of Zhou was born with the character for military prowess inscribed on his palm, and the clan took that sign as its surname.

translations.literal: In Han there was Wu Chen, who was King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, Wu Chen held the title King of Zhao.

translations.literal: Marquis Xiao of Liangzou Chen fathered De.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Xiao of Liangzou, Chen, had a son named De.

translations.literal: De fathered Zui, Marquis of Dongwu Village.
translations.idiomatic: De was followed by Zui, Marquis of Dongwu Village.

translations.literal: Zui fathered Ying, Marquis Jingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zui's son Ying was ennobled as Marquis Jingxiang.

sentences.zh: 嬰生中涓、濟陰侯山附，後以酎金國除。

translations.literal: Ying fathered a Palace Attendant and Shanfu, Marquis of Jiyin; later the marquisate was abolished for insufficient libation gold.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had two sons: one served as Palace Attendant, the other was Shanfu, Marquis of Jiyin; the fief was later revoked for failure to pay the prescribed libation offering.

sentences.zh: 山附生陳留太守、內黃侯都。

translations.literal: Shanfu fathered Du, Administrator of Chenliu and Marquis of Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wushanfu's son Du became Administrator of Chenliu and Marquis of Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 都生汝南太守宣，字文達。

translations.literal: Du fathered Xuan, Administrator of Runan, styled Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: Du was succeeded by Xuan, Administrator of Runan, courtesy name Wenda.

translations.literal: Xuan had two sons: Shang and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had two sons, Shang and Fu.

translations.literal: Fu, styled Yuanhai, was Minister of Education and Left Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, courtesy name Yuanhai, served as Minister of Education and Left Chief Clerk.

translations.literal: He fathered Jing, Magistrate of Linzhang, styled Boji.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's son Jing, courtesy name Boji, became Magistrate of Linzhang.

translations.literal: Jing fathered Lie, styled Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was followed by Lie, courtesy name Wenzhao.

translations.literal: Lie fathered Du, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, styled Yibo.
translations.idiomatic: Lie had a son Du, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, courtesy name Yibo.

sentences.zh: 篤生太常、中壘校尉悌，字周篤。

translations.literal: Du fathered Ti, Grand Master of Ceremonies and Colonel of the Central Rampart, styled Zhoudu.
translations.idiomatic: Du's son Ti held the posts of Grand Master of Ceremonies and Colonel of the Central Rampart; his courtesy name was Zhoudu.

sentences.zh: 悌生九江太守、臨潁侯端。

translations.literal: Ti fathered Duan, Administrator of Jiujiang and Marquis of Linying.
translations.idiomatic: Ti was succeeded by Duan, Administrator of Jiujiang and Marquis of Linying.

sentences.zh: 端生魏侍中、南昌侯周，周三子：陔、韶、茂。

translations.literal: Duan fathered Zhou, Wei Palace Attendant and Marquis of Nanchang; Zhou's three sons: Gai, Shao, and Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Duan's son Zhou served Wei as Palace Attendant and Marquis of Nanchang and had three sons: Gai, Shao, and Mao.

sentences.zh: 陔字元夏，晉左僕射、薛定侯。

translations.literal: Gai, styled Yuanxia, was Jin Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Marquis Ding of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Gai, courtesy name Yuanxia, became Jin Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Marquis Ding of Xue.

sentences.zh: 陔生太山太守、嗣薛侯越。

translations.literal: Gai fathered Yue, Administrator of Taishan and Heir Marquis of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's son Yue served as Administrator of Taishan and Heir Marquis of Xue.

sentences.zh: 越生威遠將軍、嗣薛侯鋪。

translations.literal: Yue fathered Pu, General Who Establishes Might in the Distance and Heir Marquis of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was followed by Pu, General Who Establishes Might in the Distance and Heir Marquis of Xue.

translations.literal: Pu fathered Gu, Crown Prince's Household Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Pu had a son Gu, who served as Crown Prince's Household Attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘏生洛州長史、歸義侯念。

translations.literal: Gu fathered Nian, Chief Clerk of Luozhou and Marquis of Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's son Nian became Chief Clerk of Luozhou and Marquis of Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 念生平北將軍、五兵尚書晉陽公洽，別封大陵縣，賜田五十頃，因居之。

translations.literal: Nian fathered Qia, General Who Pacifies the North, Director of the Five Arms and Duke of Jinyang; he was separately enfeoffed at Daling County and granted fifty qing of fields, and therefore resided there.
translations.idiomatic: Nian's son Qia rose to General Who Pacifies the North, Director of the Five Arms, and Duke of Jinyang; he received a separate enfeoffment at Daling County with a grant of fifty qing of land and made his home there.

translations.literal: He fathered Shengui, Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Qia had a son Shengui, who became Libationer.

sentences.zh: 龜生本州大中正、司徒越王長史、襲壽陽公克已。

translations.literal: Shengui fathered Keyi, Provincial Rectifier of the Origin, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Yue under the Minister of Education, and Heir Duke of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shengui's son Keyi served as Provincial Rectifier, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Yue under the Minister of Education, and Heir Duke of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 已生北齊鎮遠將軍、襲壽陽公居常。

translations.literal: Keyi fathered Juchang, Northern Qi General Who Pacifies the Distance and Heir Duke of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Keyi was succeeded by Juchang, Northern Qi General Who Pacifies the Distance and Heir Duke of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 常生後周永昌王諮議參軍儉。

translations.literal: Juchang fathered Jian, Later Zhou Staff Officer for Consultation under the Prince of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Juchang's son Jian served the Later Zhou as Staff Officer for Consultation under the Prince of Yongchang.

translations.literal: He fathered Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had a son named Hua.

translations.literal: The Wu clan had five chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Five men of the Wu clan reached the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 攸暨、攸寧、元衡、三思、承嗣。

translations.literal: Youji, Youning, Yuanheng, Sansi, and Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: They were Youji, Youning, Yuanheng, Sansi, and Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 騫騫氏出自孔子弟子閔損，字子騫，其孫文，以王父字命氏。

translations.literal: The Qian clan traces its origin to Confucius's disciple Min Sun, styled Ziqian; his grandson Wen took his grandfather's style name as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The Qian clan descended from Confucius's disciple Min Sun, courtesy name Ziqian; his grandson Wen adopted the grandfather's style name as the family surname.

sentences.zh: 後漢質帝時有騫宏，字弘伯，避地允吾，為金城別駕，封金城侯，子孫因家焉。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhi of Later Han there was Qian Hong, styled Hongbo, who took refuge at Yunwu, served as Jin Commandery Vice Director, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jincheng, and descendants therefore made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Zhi of the Later Han, Qian Hong, courtesy name Hongbo, fled to Yunwu, became Vice Director of Jin Commandery, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jincheng; his descendants settled there.

sentences.zh: 裔孫彄，晉將軍、平陽郡太守。

translations.literal: A descendant Kui was Jin general and Administrator of Pingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A later descendant named Kui served the Jin as a general and Administrator of Pingyang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Bai and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Bai and Hao.

sentences.zh: 白四世孫敬，字宗之，後魏奉朝請、金城郡守、尚書庫部郎中、征南將軍、金城侯、散騎常侍、和州刺史。

translations.literal: Jing, Bai's descendant in the fourth generation, styled Zongzhi, was Later Wei Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences, Administrator of Jincheng Commandery, Gentleman of the Revenue Section in the Masters of Writing, General Who Conquers the South, Marquis of Jincheng, Regular Attendant, and Inspector of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations after Bai came Jing, courtesy name Zongzhi, who held a string of Later Wei offices culminating in Marquis of Jincheng, Regular Attendant, and Inspector of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 一子成，裔孫行本，唐靈州都督長史。

translations.literal: One son Cheng; a descendant Xingben was Tang Chief Clerk to the Protector-General of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Cheng; a descendant Xingben served the Tang as Chief Clerk to the Protector-General of Lingzhou.

translations.literal: Kui's descendant in the fifth generation was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations after Kui came Wei.

translations.literal: The Qian clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Qian clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Weidao.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao.

translations.literal: The Shen clan traces its origin to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Shen clan descended from the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 周文王第十子聃叔季，字子揖，食采於沈，汝南平輿沈亭，即其地也，春秋魯成公八年為晉所滅。

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou's tenth son Uncle Danji, styled Ziyi, received Shen as his fief; Shen Pavilion in Pingyu, Runan, was that place; in the eighth year of Duke Cheng of Lu in the Spring and Autumn period it was destroyed by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou's tenth son, Uncle Danji, courtesy name Ziyi, held the fief of Shen at Shen Pavilion in Pingyu, Runan; the state was extinguished by Jin in 583 BCE, the eighth year of Duke Cheng of Lu.

sentences.zh: 沈子生逞，字循之，奔楚，遂為沈氏。

translations.literal: The Son of Shen fathered Cheng, styled Xunzhi, who fled to Chu and thus became the Shen clan.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's son Cheng, courtesy name Xunzhi, fled to Chu and founded the Shen clan.

sentences.zh: 生嘉，嘉字惟良，二子：尹丙、尹戊。

translations.literal: He fathered Jia; Jia, styled Weiliang, had two sons: Yinbing and Yinwu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's son Jia, courtesy name Weiliang, had two sons: Yinbing and Yinwu.

sentences.zh: 尹戊字仲達，奔楚隱於零山，為楚左司馬。

translations.literal: Yinwu, styled Zhongda, fled to Chu and concealed himself on Mount Ling, and became Chu Left Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Yinwu, courtesy name Zhongda, took refuge in Chu and lived in seclusion on Mount Ling, eventually serving as Left Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 生諸梁，諸梁字子高，亦為左司馬，食采於葉，號葉公。

translations.literal: He fathered Zhuliang; Zhuliang, styled Zigao, also became Left Minister of War, received Ye as his fief, and was styled Duke of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yinwu's son Zhuliang, courtesy name Zigao, likewise became Left Minister of War, held the fief of Ye, and was known as Duke of Ye.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yinshe and Yinwen.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yinshe and Yinwen.

sentences.zh: 尹射字脩文，為楚令尹，旬日亡去，隱于華山。

translations.literal: Yinshe, styled Xiuwen, was Chu Prime Minister; within ten days he fled and concealed himself on Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshe, courtesy name Xiuwen, briefly served as Chu Prime Minister, then within ten days vanished into seclusion on Mount Hua.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yinzhu and Yinchì.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yinzhu and Yinchì.

translations.literal: Yinchì, styled Mingyin, fathered Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Yinchì, courtesy name Mingyin, had a son Ying.

sentences.zh: 郢字文明，召為丞相，不就，生平。

translations.literal: Ying, styled Wenming, was summoned as chancellor but did not accept; he fathered Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, courtesy name Wenming, was invited to become chancellor but declined; his son was Ping.

sentences.zh: 平字俊之，封竹邑侯，生遂。

translations.literal: Ping, styled Junzhi, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuyi and fathered Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, courtesy name Junzhi, was ennobled as Marquis of Zhuyi and had a son Sui.

translations.literal: Sui, styled Zuoshi, was a Qin Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Sui, courtesy name Zuoshi, served the Qin as an Erudite.

sentences.zh: 生倧，字文甫，左庶長、竹邑侯，生遵。

translations.literal: He fathered Cong, styled Wenfu, Left Chief Grandee and Marquis of Zhuyi, who fathered Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's son Cong, courtesy name Wenfu, became Left Chief Grandee and Marquis of Zhuyi; Cong's son was Zun.

sentences.zh: 遵字伯吾，漢齊王太傅、敷德侯，徙居九江壽春。

translations.literal: Zun, styled Bowu, was Han Tutor to the King of Qi and Marquis Fude, and moved to reside at Shouchun in Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zun, courtesy name Bowu, served as Tutor to the King of Qi and was ennobled as Marquis Fude, then resettled at Shouchun in Jiujiang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Sheng and Da.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Sheng and Da.

translations.literal: Da, styled Bohong, was General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Da, courtesy name Bohong, rose to General of Agile Cavalry.

translations.literal: He fathered Qian, styled Zhongyuan, Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Da's son Qian, courtesy name Zhongyuan, became Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 生泓，泓字元良，南陽太守、彭城侯。

translations.literal: He fathered Hong; Hong, styled Yuanliang, was Administrator of Nanyang and Marquis of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Hong, courtesy name Yuanliang, served as Administrator of Nanyang and Marquis of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 生勗，勗字子衡，揚武校尉、鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: He fathered Xu; Xu, styled Ziheng, was Colonel Who Displays Military Might and General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Xu, courtesy name Ziheng, held the posts of Colonel Who Displays Military Might and General Who Pacifies the Army.

translations.literal: Three sons: Song, Fen, and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Song, Fen, and Feng.

translations.literal: Fen, styled Zhongyi, was Imperial Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Fen, courtesy name Zhongyi, served as Imperial Secretary.

sentences.zh: 生格，格字仲悌，將作大匠。

translations.literal: He fathered Ge; Ge, styled Zhongti, was Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Fen's son Ge, courtesy name Zhongti, became Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 生謙，謙字文恭，御史中丞。

translations.literal: He fathered Qian; Qian, styled Wengong, was Imperial Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Ge's son Qian, courtesy name Wengong, served as Imperial Secretary.

sentences.zh: 生靖，靖字文光，濟陰太守，避王莽之難，隱居桐柏山。

translations.literal: He fathered Jing; Jing, styled Wenguang, was Administrator of Jiyin; to avoid the troubles of Wang Mang he concealed himself on Mount Tongbai.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Jing, courtesy name Wenguang, was Administrator of Jiyin but withdrew to seclusion on Mount Tongbai to escape the turmoil of Wang Mang's reign.

translations.literal: Three sons: Xun, Rong, and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Xun, Rong, and Tai.

sentences.zh: 戎字威卿，後漢先祿勳，以九江從事降劇賊尹良，封為海昏侯，辭不就，徙居會稽之烏程。

translations.literal: Rong, styled Weiqing, was Later Han Director of Retainers; as Jiujiang Assistant he submitted to the fierce bandit Yin Liang and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Haihun but declined and did not accept, moving to reside at Wucheng in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, courtesy name Weiqing, served the Later Han as Director of Retainers; while serving in Jiujiang he submitted to the rebel Yin Liang and was offered the marquisate of Haihun, but he refused the title and settled at Wucheng in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 靈帝分烏程為永安縣，孫皓分吳郡為吳興郡，晉改永安為武康，即為郡人。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling divided off Wucheng as Yong'an County; Sun Hao divided off Wu Commandery as Wuxing Commandery; Jin changed Yong'an to Wukang, and they thereby became men of that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling carved Yong'an County out of Wucheng; Sun Hao later split Wuxing Commandery from Wu; the Jin renamed Yong'an as Wukang, and the family thereby became natives of that district.

translations.literal: Rong fathered four sons: Feng, Yi, Qi, and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had four sons: Feng, Yi, Qi, and Gong.

translations.literal: Feng, styled Shengtong, was Administrator of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, courtesy name Shengtong, became Administrator of Lingling.

translations.literal: Four sons: Hu, Zhong, Gao, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Hu, Zhong, Gao, and Jing.

translations.literal: Jing was Chancellor of Hejian and fathered Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing served as Chancellor of Hejian and had a son Yan.

translations.literal: Yan's descendant Junliang.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Yan was Junliang.

translations.literal: The Shen clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Shen clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Junliang.
translations.idiomatic: Junliang.

translations.literal: The Su clan traces its origin to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Su clan descended from the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 顓頊裔孫吳回為重黎，生陸終。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu's descendant Wu Hui was Chongli and fathered Luzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hui, a descendant of Zhuanxu, held the title Chongli and was the father of Luzhong.

translations.literal: He fathered Fan, who was enfeoffed at Kunwu.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhong's son Fan was granted the fief of Kunwu.

sentences.zh: 昆吾之子封於蘇，其地鄴西蘇城是也。

translations.literal: Kunwu's son was enfeoffed at Su; that place is Su City west of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's descendant was enfeoffed at Su, present-day Su City west of Ye.

sentences.zh: 蘇忿生為周司寇，世居河內，後徙武功杜陵，至漢代郡太守建，徙扶風平陵，封平陵侯。

translations.literal: Su Fensheng was Zhou Minister of Crime; the clan dwelt for generations in Henei, later moved to Dulang in Wugong, down to Han Administrator of Dai Commandery Jian, who moved to Pingling in Fufeng and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingling.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fensheng served Zhou as Minister of Crime; the family long resided in Henei, later moved to Dulang in Wugong, and by the Han Administrator of Dai Jian had resettled at Pingling in Fufeng and been ennobled as Marquis of Pingling.

translations.literal: Three sons: Jia, Wu, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Jia, Wu, and Xian.

translations.literal: Jia was Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Jia served as Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 六世孫南陽太守、中陵鄉侯純，字桓公。

translations.literal: Chun, Jia's descendant in the sixth generation, Administrator of Nanyang and Marquis of Zhongling Township, styled Huangong.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations after Jia came Chun, courtesy name Huangong, Administrator of Nanyang and Marquis of Zhongling Township.

translations.literal: He fathered Zhang, styled Ruwen, Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's son Zhang, courtesy name Ruwen, became Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五世孫魏東平相、都亭剛侯則，字文師。

translations.literal: Ze, Zhang's descendant in the fifth generation, Wei Chancellor of Dongping and Marquis Gang of Duting, styled Wenshi.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations after Zhang came Ze, courtesy name Wenshi, who served Wei as Chancellor of Dongping and Marquis Gang of Duting.

translations.literal: Four sons: Tian, Yu, Dun, and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Tian, Yu, Dun, and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 愉字休豫，晉太常光祿大夫、尚書。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Xiuyu, was Jin Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, courtesy name Xiuyu, held Jin posts as Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Master of Writing.

translations.literal: Tong, Yu's descendant in the seventh generation.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after Yu came Tong.

translations.literal: Two sons: Ya and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Ya and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 魏都亭剛侯則第三子遁八世孫綽，周度支尚書、邳公。

translations.literal: Chuo, Dun's descendant in the eighth generation—Dun being the third son of Wei Marquis Gang of Duting Ze—was Zhou Director of Revenue Accounts and Duke of Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo, eight generations from Dun—the third son of Wei Marquis Gang of Duting Ze—served Zhou as Director of Revenue Accounts and was ennobled as Duke of Pi.

translations.literal: He fathered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo had a son named Wei.

sentences.zh: 趙郡蘇氏出自漢幷州刺史章之後，因官居趙州。

translations.literal: The Zhaojun Su clan issued from after Han Inspector of Bingzhou Zhang, and because of office resided at Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaojun branch of the Su clan descended from Han Inspector of Bingzhou Zhang and settled in Zhao Prefecture through official service.

translations.literal: There was also the Wugong Su clan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Wugong branch of the Su clan.

translations.literal: The Su clan had five chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Five men of the Su clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Liangsi, Gui, Ting, Weidao, and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: They were Liangsi, Gui, Ting, Weidao, and Jian.

sentences.zh: 范范氏出自祁姓，帝堯裔孫劉累之後。

translations.literal: The Fan clan traces its origin to the Qi surname, after Emperor Yao's descendant Liu Lei.
translations.idiomatic: The Fan clan descended from the Qi lineage through Liu Lei, a descendant of Emperor Yao.

sentences.zh: 在周為唐杜氏，周宣王滅杜，杜伯之子隰叔奔晉為士師，曾孫士會，食采於范，其地濮州范縣也，子孫遂為范氏。

translations.literal: In Zhou they were the Tang Du clan; King Xuan of Zhou destroyed Du; Duke Du's son Xishu fled to Jin as Minister of Works; his great-grandson Shi Hui received Fan as his fief—that place is Fan County in Puzhou—and descendants therefore became the Fan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou they were known as the Tang Du clan until King Xuan destroyed Du; Duke Du's son Xishu fled to Jin as Minister of Works, and his great-grandson Shi Hui received the fief of Fan in present-day Fan County, Puzhou, from which the Fan surname derives.

sentences.zh: 至後漢博士滂，世居河內。

translations.literal: Down to Later Han Erudite Pang, they dwelt for generations in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: By the Later Han Erudite Pang, the clan had long resided in Henei.

translations.literal: In Tang there was Lubing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang the line produced Lubing.

translations.literal: The Fan clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Fan clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Lubing.
translations.idiomatic: Lubing.

translations.literal: The Xing clan traces its origin to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Xing clan descended from the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 周公第四子封於邢，後為衞所滅，子孫以國為氏。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou's fourth son was enfeoffed at Xing; later it was destroyed by Wei, and descendants took the state as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou's fourth son was granted Xing as his fief; after Wei extinguished the state, his descendants adopted the realm as their surname.

translations.literal: They dwelt for generations at Quanjiao in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The family long resided at Quanjiao in Chuzhou.

translations.literal: In Tang there was Palace Secretary Wenwei, who served as chancellor to Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, Wenwei served as Palace Secretary and chancellor to Empress Wu.

translations.literal: The Xing clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Xing clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Wenwei.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei.

translations.literal: The Fu clan traces its origin to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu clan descended from the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 黃帝裔孫大由封於傅邑，因以為氏。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor's descendant Dayou was enfeoffed at Fu, and therefore took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Dayou, a descendant of the Yellow Emperor, was granted the fief of Fu and adopted that place as the clan surname.

sentences.zh: 商時虞、虢之界，有傅氏居于巖傍，號為傅巖。

translations.literal: In Shang times on the border of Yu and Guo, the Fu clan dwelt beside a cliff and were styled Fu Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shang, on the border between Yu and Guo, a Fu clan lived beside a cliff and gave their settlement the name Fu Cliff.

sentences.zh: 盤庚得說於此，命以為相。

translations.literal: Pan Geng obtained Yue here and appointed him as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Geng found Yue at this place and made him chancellor.

sentences.zh: 裔孫漢義陽侯介子始居北地。

translations.literal: A descendant, Han Marquis of Yiyang Jiezi, first dwelt in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: A scion of the line, Jiezi, Marquis of Yiyang under Han, first settled in Beidi.

translations.literal: His great-grandson Changfu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Changfu was invested as Marquis of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 生章，章生叡，叡生後漢弘農太守允，字固。

translations.literal: He fathered Zhang; Zhang fathered Rui; Rui fathered Yun, styled Gu, Later Han Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was his son; Rui was Zhang's son; and Rui's son Yun, courtesy name Gu, became Administrator of Hongnong under the Later Han.

translations.literal: Two sons: Gu and Song.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Gu and Song.

sentences.zh: 嘏字蘭石，魏尚書僕射、陽都元侯。

translations.literal: Gu, styled Lanshi, was Wei Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Marquis Yuan of Yangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, courtesy name Lanshi, served Wei as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and was ennobled as Marquis Yuan of Yangdu.

sentences.zh: 十一世孫弈，唐中散大夫、太史令、泥陽縣男。

translations.literal: An eleventh-generation descendant, Yi, was Tang Palace Attendant, Grand Astrologer, and Baron of Niyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh generation, Yi held the Tang offices of Palace Attendant and Grand Astrologer and bore the title Baron of Niyang.

sentences.zh: 北齊有行臺僕射傅伏武，孫文傑，唐杞王府典軍。

translations.literal: In Northern Qi there was Fu Fuwu, Deputy Director of the Mobile Administration; his grandson Wenjie was Tang Colonel of the Qi Princely Household.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Qi, Fu Fuwu served as Deputy Director of the Mobile Administration; his grandson Wenjie became Colonel of the Qi Princely Household in Tang.

sentences.zh: 清河傅氏出自後漢漢陽太守壯節侯燮，字南容。

translations.literal: The Qinghe Fu clan descended from Xie, styled Nanrong, Later Han Administrator of Hanyang and Marquis Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu of Qinghe traced their descent to Xie, courtesy name Nanrong, Administrator of Hanyang and Marquis Zhuangjie under the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 生幹，字彥林，魏扶風太守。

translations.literal: He fathered Gan, styled Yanlin, Wei Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gan, courtesy name Yanlin, Administrator of Fufeng under Wei.

sentences.zh: 生晉司隸校尉、鶉觚剛侯玄，字休弈，生司隸校尉、貞侯咸，子孫自北地徙清河。

translations.literal: He fathered Xuan, styled Xiuyi, Jin Director of the Metropolitan Region and Marquis Gang of Chunggu; Xuan fathered Xian, Director of the Metropolitan Region and Marquis Zhen; descendants moved from Beidi to Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, courtesy name Xiuyi, served Jin as Director of the Metropolitan Region and Marquis Gang of Chunggu; his son Xian also held the directorship and bore the title Marquis Zhen. The line later moved from Beidi to Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 裔孫仕後魏為南陽太守，生交益。

translations.literal: A descendant served Later Wei as Administrator of Nanyang and fathered Jiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: A scion of the line entered Later Wei service as Administrator of Nanyang and had a son Jiaoyi.

translations.literal: The Fu clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Fu clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Youyi.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi.

sentences.zh: 史史氏出自周太史佚之後，子孫以官為氏。

translations.literal: The Shi clan descended from Yi, Grand Historian of Zhou; descendants took the office as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi clan traced their line to Yi, Grand Historian of Zhou, and later generations adopted his office as their surname.

translations.literal: In Han there was Shi Gong of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han there was Shi Gong of Lu.

translations.literal: Three sons: Gao, Zeng, and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Gao, Zeng, and Xuan.

translations.literal: Gao was Grand Marshal and Marquis An of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Gao rose to Grand Marshal and was enfeoffed as Marquis An of Leling.

translations.literal: Two sons: Shu and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Shu and Dan.

translations.literal: Dan was General of the Left and Marquis Qing of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dan served as General of the Left and bore the title Marquis Qing of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 孫均，均子崇，自杜陵受封溧陽侯，遂為郡人。

translations.literal: His grandson was Jun; Jun's son Chong received enfeoffment as Marquis of Liyang from Duling and thus became a man of that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Jun, and Jun's son Chong, enfeoffed at Duling as Marquis of Liyang, thereafter made his home in that commandery.

translations.literal: A descendant of Chong, Gui, was Magistrate of Lexiang in Song.
translations.idiomatic: A scion of Chong's line, Gui, served Song as Magistrate of Lexiang.

translations.literal: The Shi clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Shi clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzi.

translations.literal: The Zong clan descended from the Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Zong clan traced their descent to the Zi lineage.

sentences.zh: 宋襄公母弟敖仕晉，孫伯宗為三卿所殺，子州犂奔楚，食采於鍾離。

translations.literal: Ao, younger uterine brother of Duke Xiang of Song, served Jin; his grandson Bozong was killed by the Three Ministers; his son Zhouli fled to Chu and received a fief at Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Ao, Duke Xiang of Song's younger uterine brother, entered Jin's service; his grandson Bozong was slain by the Three Ministers, and Bozong's son Zhouli fled to Chu, where he received a fief at Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 州犂少子連，家於南陽，以王父字為氏，世居河東。

translations.literal: Zhouli's youngest son Lian established his household in Nanyang, took his grandfather's courtesy name as surname, and dwelt for generations in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouli's youngest son Lian settled in Nanyang, took his grandfather's courtesy name as the clan surname, and the family remained for generations in Hedong.

translations.literal: The Zong clan had two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Two men of the Zong clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Qinke and Chuke.
translations.idiomatic: Qinke and Chuke.

translations.literal: The Ge clan descended from Yunge.
translations.idiomatic: The Ge clan traced their descent to Yunge.

translations.literal: In Han there was Ban the Censor; a descendant was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han there was Ban the Censor; a scion of his line was Xian.

translations.literal: The Ge clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Ge clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Fuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan.

translations.literal: The Ouyang clan descended from the Si surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Ouyang clan traced their descent to the Si lineage.

sentences.zh: 夏少康庶子封于會稽，至越王無彊為楚所滅，無彊子蹄更封於烏程歐餘山之陽，為歐陽亭侯，遂以為氏。

translations.literal: A secondary son of Shao Kang of Xia was enfeoffed at Kuaiji; when King Wujiang of Yue was destroyed by Chu, Wujiang's son Ti was again enfeoffed on the south slope of Ouyu Mountain at Wucheng as Marquis of Ouyang Pavilion, and thus took it as surname.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary son of Shao Kang of Xia received Kuaiji as his fief; when King Wujiang of Yue fell to Chu, Wujiang's son Ti was enfeoffed anew on the southern slope of Ouyu Mountain at Wucheng as Marquis of Ouyang Pavilion, and from that title the clan took its name.

sentences.zh: 後有為涿郡太守，子孫或居渤海。

translations.literal: Later one served as Administrator of Zhuo Commandery; some descendants dwelt in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Later a member of the line served as Administrator of Zhuo Commandery, and some descendants settled in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 晉頓丘太守建為趙王所殺，兄子質，字純之，居長沙臨湘。

translations.literal: Jian, Jin Administrator of Dunqiu, was killed by the Prince of Zhao; his brother's son Zhi, styled Chunzhi, dwelt in Linxiang, Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Administrator of Dunqiu under Jin, was put to death by the Prince of Zhao; his brother's son Zhi, courtesy name Chunzhi, made his home in Linxiang in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 七世族孫景達，字敬遠，齊本州治中。

translations.literal: A seventh-generation clansman, Jingda, styled Jingyuan, was Aide of the Prefecture in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh generation of the clan, Jingda, courtesy name Jingyuan, served Qi as Aide of the Prefecture.

translations.literal: He fathered Sengbao, styled Shizhang, Magistrate of Lipu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Sengbao, courtesy name Shizhang, Magistrate of Lipu.

sentences.zh: 僧寶生梁陽山穆公頠，字靖世。

translations.literal: Sengbao fathered Yi, Duke Mu of Yangshan in Liang, styled Jingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbao fathered Yi, styled Jingshi, who was enfeoffed in Liang as Duke Mu of Yangshan.

translations.literal: Yi had two sons: He and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had two sons: He and Yue.

translations.literal: The Ouyang clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Ouyang clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Tong.

translations.literal: The Di clan descended from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Di clan traced their descent to the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 周成王母弟孝伯封於狄城，因以為氏。

translations.literal: Xiaobo, younger uterine brother of King Cheng of Zhou, was enfeoffed at Dicheng and thus took it as surname.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo, King Cheng of Zhou's younger uterine brother, received Dicheng as his fief and took that place as the clan surname.

sentences.zh: 孔子弟子狄黑裔孫漢博士山，世居天水。

translations.literal: From Di He, disciple of Confucius, descended Shan, an Erudite in Han, whose family dwelt for generations in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: From Di He, a disciple of Confucius, descended Shan, an Erudite under Han, whose family long resided in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 後秦樂平侯伯支裔孫恭，居太原，生湛，東魏帳內正都督、臨邑子。

translations.literal: Gong, a descendant of Bozhi, Marquis of Leping in Later Qin, dwelt in Taiyuan; he fathered Zhan, Eastern Wei Chief Commander of the Inner Guard and Viscount of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, a scion of Bozhi, Marquis of Leping under Later Qin, settled in Taiyuan and fathered Zhan, Chief Commander of the Inner Guard under Eastern Wei and Viscount of Linyi.

translations.literal: His grandson Xiaoxu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Xiaoxu.

translations.literal: The Di clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Di clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Renjie.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie.

translations.literal: The Yuan clan traces its origin to the Gui surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan descended from the Gui lineage.

sentences.zh: 陳胡公滿生申公犀侯，犀侯生靖伯庚，庚生季子惽，惽生仲牛甫，甫生聖伯順，順生伯他父，他父生戴伯，戴伯生鄭叔，鄭叔生仲爾金父，金父生莊伯，莊伯生諸，字伯爰，孫宣仲濤塗，賜邑陽夏，以王父字為氏。

translations.literal: Duke Hu of Chen Man fathered Shen Gong Xi Hou, Jing Bo Geng, Ji Zi Min, Zhong Niu Fu, Sheng Bo Shun, Bo Ta Fu, Dai Bo, Zheng Shu, Zhong Er Jin Fu, and Zhuang Bo; Zhuang Bo's son Zhu, styled Bo Yuan, was succeeded by his grandson Xuan Zhong Tao Tu, who was granted Yangxia and took his grandfather's style name as the clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Man, Duke Hu of Chen, was followed by Shen Gong Xi Hou, Jing Bo Geng, Ji Zi Min, Zhong Niu Fu, Sheng Bo Shun, Bo Ta Fu, Dai Bo, Zheng Shu, Zhong Er Jin Fu, and Zhuang Bo. Zhuang Bo's son Zhu, courtesy name Bo Yuan, was succeeded by his grandson Xuan Zhong Tao Tu, who received the estate of Yangxia and adopted his grandfather's style name as the family surname.

sentences.zh: 宣仲生選，選生聲子突，突生惠子雅，雅生頗，奔鄭。

translations.literal: Xuan Zhong fathered Xuan; Xuan fathered Sheng Zi Tu; Tu fathered Hui Zi Ya; Ya fathered Po, who fled to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: From Xuan Zhong came Xuan, then Sheng Zi Tu, Hui Zi Ya, and Ya's son Po, who fled to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 秦末，裔孫告辟難居于河、洛之間，少子政，以袁為氏。

translations.literal: At the end of Qin, a descendant Gong took refuge from turmoil and settled between the Yellow and Luo Rivers; his youngest son Zheng took Yuan as the clan name.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Qin, a descendant named Gong fled the chaos and settled between the Yellow and Luo Rivers; his youngest son Zheng adopted Yuan as the family name.

translations.literal: The ninth-generation descendant Yuan Sheng fathered Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth generation, Yuan Sheng was followed by Xuan.

sentences.zh: 孫幹，封貴鄉侯，復居陳郡陽夏。

translations.literal: His descendant Gan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guixiang and again settled in Yangxia, Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant, Gan, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guixiang and returned to Yangxia in Chen Commandery.

translations.literal: The eighth-generation descendant Liang had two sons: Chang and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth generation, Liang had two sons, Chang and Zhang.

sentences.zh: 昌，成武令，生漢司徒安，字邵公。

translations.literal: Chang, Magistrate of Chengwu, fathered An, Han Minister over the Masses, styled Duke Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, magistrate of Chengwu, was the father of An, Minister over the Masses under Han, courtesy name Duke Shao.

translations.literal: Three sons: Shang, Jing, and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Shang, Jing, and Chang.

translations.literal: Jing, Administrator of Shu Commandery, had two sons: Peng and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Administrator of Shu Commandery, had two sons, Peng and Tang.

sentences.zh: 湯字仲河，太尉、安國康侯。

translations.literal: Tang, styled Zhonghe, was Grand Commandant and Marquis Kang of Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, courtesy name Zhonghe, served as Grand Commandant and was enfeoffed as Marquis Kang of Anguo.

translations.literal: Three sons: Cheng, Feng, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Cheng, Feng, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 成，左中郎，生紹，紹中子熙，其後世居樂陵東光。

translations.literal: Cheng, Left Gentleman, fathered Shao; Shao's second son was Xi; his descendants afterward dwelt in Dongguang, Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, a Left Gentleman, had a son Shao, whose second son was Xi; that branch later settled in Dongguang, Leling.

translations.literal: A descendant of Xi, Lingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Among Xi's descendants was Lingxi.

translations.literal: Zhang fathered Pang, Minister over the Masses, styled Duke Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was the father of Pang, Minister over the Masses, courtesy name Duke Xi.

sentences.zh: 滂生渙，字曜卿，魏御史大夫。

translations.literal: Pang fathered Huan, styled Yaoging, Wei Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Pang's son Huan, courtesy name Yaoging, served as Grand Censor under Wei.

translations.literal: Four sons: Kan, Yu, Ao, and Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Kan, Yu, Ao, and Zhun.

translations.literal: Zhun, styled Xiaoni, was Jin Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun, courtesy name Xiaoni, served as Supervising Censor under Jin.

translations.literal: He fathered Chong, styled Jingxuan, Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong, courtesy name Jingxuan, held the office of Director of the Imperial Household.

translations.literal: He fathered Dan, styled Yandao, Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was followed by Dan, courtesy name Yandao, Administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 耽生質，字道和，東陽太守。

translations.literal: Dan fathered Zhi, styled Daohé, Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's son Zhi, courtesy name Daohé, served as Administrator of Dongyang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhan and Bao.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zhan and Bao.

translations.literal: Bao, styled Shiwei, was Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, courtesy name Shiwei, served as Governor of Danyang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xun and Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xun and Zhan.

translations.literal: Xun, Song Administrator of Wu Commandery, was posthumously titled Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Administrator of Wu Commandery under Song, was posthumously honored with the title Zhen.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yi and Qi.

translations.literal: Yi, styled Guozhang, was Song Inspector-General of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, courtesy name Guozhang, served as Inspector-General of Yong Province under Song.

translations.literal: Two sons: Ji and Ang.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Ji and Ang.

translations.literal: The Yuan of Hedong originally issued from Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan of Hedong originally stemmed from Chen Commandery.

translations.literal: The Yuan clan had three chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Three men of the Yuan clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Shuji, Zi, and Zhihong.
translations.idiomatic: They were Shuji, Zi, and Zhihong.

sentences.zh: 姚姚姓，虞舜生於姚墟，因以為姓。

translations.literal: The Yao surname: Yu Shun was born at Yao Ru and therefore took it as his surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao clan takes its name from Yao Ru, where Yu Shun was born.

sentences.zh: 陳胡公裔孫敬仲仕齊為田氏，其後居魯，至田豐，王莽封為代睦侯，以奉舜後。

translations.literal: A descendant of Duke Hu of Chen, Jing Zhong, entered service in Qi and became of the Tian clan; his descendants later dwelt in Lu; reaching Tian Feng, Wang Mang enfeoffed him as Marquis of Daimu to maintain the line of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Zhong, a descendant of Duke Hu of Chen, entered Qi and took the surname Tian; his line later settled in Lu. Tian Feng was enfeoffed by Wang Mang as Marquis of Daimu to preserve the sacrificial line of Shun.

sentences.zh: 子恢避莽亂，過江居吳郡，改姓為媯。

translations.literal: His son Hui avoided the turmoil of Wang Mang, crossed the river, and settled in Wu Commandery, changing his surname to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui fled Wang Mang's upheaval, crossed the Yangzi, and settled in Wu Commandery, changing the family name back to Gui.

sentences.zh: 五世孫敷，復改姓姚，居吳興武康。

translations.literal: The fifth-generation descendant Fu again changed his surname to Yao and dwelt in Wukang, Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later, Fu restored the surname Yao and settled in Wukang, Wuxing.

translations.literal: Fu fathered Xin, Wu Director of Selection.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's son Xin served as Director of Selection under Wu.

sentences.zh: 八世孫僧垣，隋開府儀同三司、北隆公。

translations.literal: The eighth-generation descendant Sengyuan was Sui Commissioner with the Rank of Opening the Fu with Equal Third Rank and Duke of Beilong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth generation, Sengyuan held the rank of Commissioner with the Rank of Opening the Fu with Equal Third Rank under Sui and was enfeoffed as Duke of Beilong.

translations.literal: Two sons: Cha and Zui.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Cha and Zui.

translations.literal: The Yao of Shaan Commandery also issued from Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao clan of Shaan Commandery likewise traced its origin to Wukang.

sentences.zh: 梁有征東將軍吳興郡公宣業，生安仁，隋汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Liang there was Xuanye, General Who Conquers the East and Duke of Wuxing Commandery, who fathered Anren, Sui Governor of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang, Xuanye, General Who Conquers the East and Duke of Wuxing Commandery, was the father of Anren, Governor of Fen Prefecture under Sui.

translations.literal: He fathered Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was followed by Xiang.

translations.literal: The Yao clan had two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Two men of the Yao clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Shu and Yuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: They were Shu and Yuanzhi.

translations.literal: The Lou clan descended from the Si surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Lou clan traced its descent to the Si lineage.

sentences.zh: 夏少康裔孫東樓公封於𣏌，為楚所滅，子孫食邑於婁，因以為氏，城陽諸縣有婁鄉是也。

translations.literal: A descendant of Xia Shaokang, Duke of Donglou, was enfeoffed at Qi; when Chu destroyed it, his descendants fed upon the fief of Lou and therefore took it as their clan name; Lou Township in the counties around Chengyang is that place.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Donglou, a descendant of Shaokang of Xia, was enfeoffed at Qi; after Chu overthrew the state, his descendants lived on the fief of Lou and took that name. Lou Township in the Chengyang region marks the site.

translations.literal: The Lou clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Lou clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Shide.
translations.idiomatic: Shide.

sentences.zh: 豆盧豆盧氏本姓慕容氏。

translations.literal: The Doulu clan originally bore the surname Murong.
translations.idiomatic: The Doulu clan was originally of the Murong surname.

sentences.zh: 燕主廆弟西平王運生尚書令臨澤敬侯制，制生右衞將軍北地愍王精，降後魏，北人謂歸義為「豆盧」，因賜以為氏，居昌黎棘城。

translations.literal: Yun, younger brother of the Yan ruler Hui and Prince of Xiping, fathered Zhi, Minister-in-Chief and Marquis Jing of Linze; Zhi fathered Jing, Right Guard General and Prince Min of Beidi, who surrendered to Later Wei; northerners called surrender Doulu, and he was granted that as his clan name, dwelling at Jicheng in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Xiping and younger brother of the Yan ruler Hui, was followed by Zhi, Minister-in-Chief and Marquis Jing of Linze, and then by Jing, Right Guard General and Prince Min of Beidi. When Jing surrendered to Later Wei, the northerners called such submission Doulu, and that word was granted to him as a surname; his line settled at Jicheng in Changli.

translations.literal: Two sons: Chou and Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Chou and Sheng.

translations.literal: The Doulu clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Doulu clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Qinwang.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang.

translations.literal: The Zhou clan descended from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou clan traced their descent to the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 黃帝裔孫后稷，后稷封於邰，其地扶風斄鄉是也。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor's descendant Hou Ji was enfeoffed at Tai; that place is Leixiang in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji, a descendant of the Yellow Emperor, received Tai as his fief at present-day Leixiang in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 后稷子不窋失其官，竄於西戎，曾孫慶節，立國於豳，其地新平漆縣東北有豳亭是也。

translations.literal: Hou Ji's son Buzhu lost his office and fled among the Western Rong; his great-grandson Qingjie established a state at Bin, that place being Bin Pavilion northeast of Qixian in Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji's son Buzhu lost his post and took refuge among the Western Rong; four generations later Qingjie founded a state at Bin, northeast of Qixian in Xinping.

sentences.zh: 七世孫古公亶父，為狄所逼，徙居岐下之周原，改國號曰周，其地扶風美陽南是也。

translations.literal: The seventh-generation descendant Gugong Danfu, pressed by the Di, moved to Zhou Plain below Qi and changed the state name to Zhou; that place is south of Meiyang in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations later Gugong Danfu, harried by the Di, resettled on Zhou Plain below Qi, renamed the realm Zhou, and made his seat south of Meiyang in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 武王克商，十一世平王遷都王城，河南縣是也。

translations.literal: King Wu conquered Shang; in the eleventh generation King Ping moved the capital to Wangcheng, which is Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wu overthrew Shang, the eleventh-generation King Ping transferred the capital to Wangcheng in Henan.

translations.literal: King Ping's youngest son Lie received the fief of Rufen.
translations.idiomatic: King Ping's youngest son Lie held the fief of Rufen.

sentences.zh: 烈生懋，懋生文，文生昇，昇生興，興生晏，晏生安，安生弘，弘生明，明生隱，隱生壽，壽生容，容生休，休生雄，雄生暉，暉生寬，寬生員，員生成，成生邕。

translations.literal: Lie fathered Mao, Mao fathered Wen, Wen fathered Sheng, Sheng fathered Xing, Xing fathered Yan, Yan fathered An, An fathered Hong, Hong fathered Ming, Ming fathered Yin, Yin fathered Shou, Shou fathered Rong, Rong fathered Xiu, Xiu fathered Xiong, Xiong fathered Hui, Hui fathered Kuan, Kuan fathered Yuan, Yuan fathered Cheng, Cheng fathered Yong.
translations.idiomatic: From Lie through Mao, Wen, Sheng, Xing, Yan, An, Hong, Ming, Yin, Shou, Rong, Xiu, Xiong, Hui, Kuan, Yuan, and Cheng, the line descended to Yong.

sentences.zh: 秦滅周，幷其地，遂為汝南著姓。

translations.literal: Qin destroyed Zhou and annexed its territory, and they thereby became a prominent surname of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin extinguished Zhou and annexed its lands, the family became a leading clan of Runan.

translations.literal: He fathered Xiu; Xiu fathered Ren, styled Jifang.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Xiu was followed by Ren, courtesy name Jifang.

sentences.zh: 漢興，續周之嗣，復封為汝墳侯，賜號正公。

translations.literal: When Han arose, continuing Zhou's succession, he was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Rufen and granted the title Lord Correct.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han the line was recognized as Zhou's heirs, re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Rufen, and granted the title Lord Correct.

translations.literal: Because Rufen was low and wet, he moved to Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because Rufen was damp and low-lying, the seat was moved to Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 十子，長曰球，執金吾，生平陵令應。

translations.literal: Ten sons; the eldest was Qiu, Bearer of the Mace, who fathered Ying, Magistrate of Pingling.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons; the eldest, Qiu, Bearer of the Mace, fathered Ying, Magistrate of Pingling.

sentences.zh: 應生郎中、孝廉道，道生五官中郎約，約生決曹掾燕，燕裔孫表。

translations.literal: Ying fathered Dao, Gentleman and Filial and Incorrupt; Dao fathered Yue, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; Yue fathered Yan, Clerk of the Decision Section; Yan's descendant was Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's son Dao, a Gentleman nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, was followed by Yue of the Masters of Writing, then Yan as Clerk of the Decision Section, and later Biao.

sentences.zh: 永安周氏亦出自決曹掾燕。

translations.literal: The Yong'an Zhou clan also issued from Yan, Clerk of the Decision Section.
translations.idiomatic: The Yong'an branch of the Zhou clan likewise descended from Yan, Clerk of the Decision Section.

sentences.zh: 九世孫防，防十三世孫靈超。

translations.literal: The ninth-generation descendant Fang; Fang's thirteenth-generation descendant Lingchao.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations later came Fang; thirteen generations after Fang came Lingchao.

sentences.zh: 其先避西晉之亂，南徙居永安黃岡。

translations.literal: His forebears, fleeing the turmoil of Western Jin, moved south and settled at Huangang in Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors fled Western Jin's turmoil and migrated south to Huangang in Yong'an.

translations.literal: The Zhou clan had two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Two men of the Zhou clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Yunyuan and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: They were Yunyuan and Chi.

translations.literal: The Ji clan descended from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji clan traced their descent to the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 黃帝裔孫伯儵封於南燕，賜姓曰姞，其地東郡燕縣是也，後改為吉。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor's descendant Bosu was enfeoffed at Southern Yan and granted the surname Ji; that place is Yan County in Dong Commandery, later changed to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bosu, a descendant of the Yellow Emperor, was granted Southern Yan and the surname Ji at present-day Yan County in Dong Commandery; the name was later changed to Ji.

translations.literal: The Ji clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Ji clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu.

translations.literal: The Gu clan descended from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Gu clan traced their descent to the Ji lineage.

sentences.zh: 顧伯，夏商侯國也，子孫以國為氏，初居會稽。

translations.literal: The state of Gu Bo was a Xia and Shang marquisate; descendants took the state as their clan name and first dwelt in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bo had been a feudatory state under Xia and Shang; descendants adopted the realm as their surname and first settled in Kuaiji.

translations.literal: Wu Chancellor Yong's grandson Rong was Jin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, grandson of Wu Chancellor Yong, served Jin as Minister of Works.

translations.literal: Yong's younger brother Hui was Palace Attendant and again resided at Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's younger brother Hui served as Palace Attendant, and another branch settled at Yanguan.

sentences.zh: 徽十世孫越，陳黃門侍郎，孫胤。

translations.literal: Hui's tenth-generation descendant Yue was Chen Vice Director of the Secretariat; his grandson Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Ten generations after Hui came Yue, Chen Vice Director of the Secretariat, and his grandson Yin.

translations.literal: The Gu clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Gu clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Cong.

translations.literal: The Zhu clan descended from the Cao surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu clan traced their descent to the Cao lineage.

sentences.zh: 顓頊之後有六終，彥六子，其第五子曰安。

translations.literal: After Zhuanxu there was Liu Zhong; Yan had six sons, and the fifth was named An.
translations.idiomatic: A line after Zhuanxu produced Liu Zhong; Yan's six sons included a fifth son named An.

sentences.zh: 周武王克商，封安苗裔俠於邾，附庸于魯，其地魯國鄒縣是也。

translations.literal: When King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang, he enfeoffed An's descendant Xie at Zhu as a dependency of Lu; that place is Zou County in the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wu of Zhou overthrew Shang, he enfeoffed Xie, a descendant of An, at Zhu as a dependency of Lu in present-day Zou County.

sentences.zh: 自安至儀父十二世，始見春秋。

translations.literal: From An down to Yifu was twelve generations before they first appeared in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve generations passed from An to Yifu before the line first appears in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 齊桓行霸，儀父附從，進爵稱子，桓公以下，春秋後八世而為楚所滅，故子孫去「邑」為朱氏，世居沛國相縣。

translations.literal: When Duke Huan of Qi exercised hegemony, Yifu followed and was advanced to the rank of viscount; after Duke Huan, eight generations later Chu destroyed the state, and descendants therefore dropped the place element from Zhu to become the Zhu clan, dwelling for generations at Xiang County in Pei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Huan of Qi rose as hegemon, Yifu followed him and was raised to viscount; eight generations after Huan, Chu extinguished Zhu, and the survivors dropped the place-name element from their written surname, becoming the Zhu clan settled at Xiang in Pei.

sentences.zh: 前漢大司馬長史詡生浮，字公叔，大司馬、大司空、新息侯。

translations.literal: Former Han Grand Marshal Chief Clerk Xu fathered Fu, styled Gongshu, Grand Marshal, Grand Minister of Works, and Marquis of Xinxie.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Han, Chief Clerk Xu of the Grand Marshal fathered Fu, courtesy name Gongshu, who rose to Grand Marshal and Grand Minister of Works and was ennobled as Marquis of Xinxie.

sentences.zh: 生下邳太守永，永九世孫吏部尚書尚，尚生質，司徒。

translations.literal: He fathered Yong, Administrator of Xiapi; Yong's ninth-generation descendant Shang, Director of the Masters of Writing; Shang fathered Zhi, Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's son Yong became Administrator of Xiapi; nine generations later Shang served as Director of the Masters of Writing; Shang's son Zhi became Minister of Education.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yu and Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yu and Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 禹，司隸校尉、青州刺史，坐黨錮誅，子孫避難丹楊，丹楊朱氏之祖也。

translations.literal: Yu was Director of the Metropolitan Region and Inspector of Qingzhou; executed in the Partisan Proscriptions; descendants took refuge in Danyang and became ancestors of the Danyang Zhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu served as Director of the Metropolitan Region and Inspector of Qingzhou but was executed in the Partisan Proscriptions; his descendants fled to Danyang and founded the Danyang Zhu line.

sentences.zh: 卓生扶風太守飜，飜生上洛太守越，越字元勝。

translations.literal: Zhuo fathered Fan, Administrator of Fufeng; Fan fathered Yue, Administrator of Shangluo; Yue, styled Yuansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's son Fan became Administrator of Fufeng; Fan's son Yue, courtesy name Yuansheng, served as Administrator of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 越八世孫丞相行參軍詢。

translations.literal: Yue's eighth-generation descendant Xun, Staff Officer in the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations after Yue came Xun, Staff Officer in the Chancellor's Office.

sentences.zh: 二子濟，濟生沖，沖生威則，散騎常侍、給事中。

translations.literal: Two sons Ji; Ji fathered Chong; Chong fathered Weize, Regular Attendant and Supervising Censor.
