translations.idiomatic: He had two sons; Ji fathered Chong, and Chong's son Weize served as Regular Attendant and Supervising Censor.

translations.literal: He fathered Teng, styled Longhuai, Administrator of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Weize's son Teng, courtesy name Longhuai, became Administrator of Chen Commandery.

translations.literal: Three sons: Xian, Bin, and Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Xian, Bin, and Chuo.

translations.literal: Chuo, styled Zuming, was Administrator of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo, courtesy name Zuming, served as Administrator of Xiyang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Lingshi and Chaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Lingshi and Chaoshi.

sentences.zh: 騰裔孫建，後周太子洗馬。

translations.literal: A descendant of Teng, Jian, was Later Zhou Crown Prince's Household Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Teng, Jian, served the Later Zhou as Crown Prince's Household Attendant.

translations.literal: He fathered Sengning, Sui Administrator of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Sengning became Administrator of Suiyang under Sui.

translations.literal: He fathered Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Sengning was followed by Cao.

translations.literal: The Zhu clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Zhu clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze.

translations.literal: The Tang clan descended from the Qi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang clan traced their descent to the Qi lineage.

sentences.zh: 帝堯初封唐侯，其地中山唐縣是也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yao was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Tang; that place is Tang County in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Tang at present-day Tang County in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 舜封堯子丹朱為唐侯，至夏時，丹朱裔孫劉累遷于魯縣，累孫猶守故地，至商，更號豕韋氏，周復改為唐公。

translations.literal: Shun enfeoffed Yao's son Danzhu as Marquis of Tang; by Xia times Danzhu's descendant Liu Lei moved to Lu County; Lei's descendants still held the old territory; in Shang it was again styled Zhuxiang Wei; in Zhou it was changed back to Duke of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Shun enfeoffed Yao's son Danzhu as Marquis of Tang; under Xia, Danzhu's descendant Liu Lei moved to Lu County while a branch kept the old seat; under Shang the line was restyled Zhuxiang Wei, and under Zhou it became Duke of Tang again.

sentences.zh: 成王滅唐，以封弟叔虞，其後更封劉累裔孫在魯縣者為唐侯，以奉堯嗣，其地唐州方城是也。

translations.literal: King Cheng destroyed Tang and enfeoffed his younger brother Uncle Yu; later he again enfeoffed Liu Lei's descendant at Lu County as Marquis of Tang to maintain Yao's succession; that place is Fangcheng in Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng extinguished Tang and granted it to his younger brother Uncle Yu; later he re-enfeoffed Liu Lei's descendant at Lu County as Marquis of Tang to preserve Yao's sacrifices at Fangcheng in Tang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 魯定公五年，楚滅唐，子孫以國為氏，分仕晉、楚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Duke Ding of Lu, Chu destroyed Tang, and descendants took the state as their clan name, serving separately in Jin and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In 509 BCE, the fifth year of Duke Ding of Lu, Chu overthrew Tang; descendants adopted the realm as their surname and entered service in Jin and Chu.

translations.literal: There was Tang Ju, a Wei grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was Tang Ju, a grandee of Wei.

sentences.zh: 孫厲，居沛國，漢封斥丘懿侯。

translations.literal: His grandson Li dwelt in Pei Commandery and was enfeoffed under Han as Marquis Yi of Chixiu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Li settled in Pei and was enfeoffed under Han as Marquis Yi of Chixiu.

sentences.zh: 生朝，朝生賢，賢生遵，遵生蒙，中郎將。

translations.literal: He fathered Chao; Chao fathered Xian; Xian fathered Zun; Zun fathered Meng, General of the Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Li's son Chao was followed by Xian, Zun, and Zun's son Meng, a General of the Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 生臨邛令都，都生倫，倫生林。

translations.literal: He fathered Du, Magistrate of Linqiong; Du fathered Lun; Lun fathered Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Meng's son Du, Magistrate of Linqiong, was followed by Lun and Lin.

sentences.zh: 林，尚書令，王莽封建德侯。

translations.literal: Lin was Director of the Masters of Writing; Wang Mang enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Lin served as Director of the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed by Wang Mang as Marquis of Jiande.

translations.literal: He fathered Wei; the state was abolished, and they moved to reside in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's son Wei, after the fief was revoked, resettled in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 生武威長惠，惠生侍御史賁，賁生大司空珍，珍生會稽太守瑁，瑁生翔，為丹楊太守，因家焉。

translations.literal: He fathered Hui, Chief of Wuwei; Hui fathered Ben, Imperial Censor; Ben fathered Zhen, Grand Minister of Works; Zhen fathered Mao, Administrator of Kuaiji; Mao fathered Xiang, who became Administrator of Danyang and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son Hui became Chief of Wuwei; Hui's son Ben served as Imperial Censor; Ben's son Zhen rose to Grand Minister of Works; Zhen's son Mao was Administrator of Kuaiji; Mao's son Xiang became Administrator of Danyang and settled there.

translations.literal: Two sons: Gu and Pang.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Gu and Pang.

translations.literal: Gu was Wu Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gu served Wu as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 生別部司馬瓊，瓊生宣，宣生晉鎮西校尉上庸襄侯彬，字儒宗。

translations.literal: He fathered Qiong, Deputy Marshal of the Separate Command; Qiong fathered Xuan; Xuan fathered Bin, Jin Colonel of the Garrison West and Marquis Xiang of Shangyong, styled Ruzong.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's son Qiong, Deputy Marshal of the Separate Command, was followed by Xuan and Bin, courtesy name Ruzong, Jin Colonel of the Garrison West and Marquis Xiang of Shangyong.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xi and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xi and Ji.

sentences.zh: 熙，太常丞，娶涼州刺史張軌女，永嘉末，遂居涼州。

translations.literal: Xi was Assistant Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and married the daughter of Liangzhou Inspector Zhang Gui; at the end of the Yongjia era he therefore dwelt in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi served as Assistant Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and married the daughter of Liangzhou Inspector Zhang Gui; at the end of the Yongjia turmoil the family settled in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 生輝，字子產，仕前涼陵江將軍，徙居晉昌。

translations.literal: He fathered Hui, styled Zichan, who served Former Liang as General of the Lingjiang Army and moved to reside in Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Hui, courtesy name Zichan, served Former Liang as General of the Lingjiang Army and resettled in Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 七子：伯廉、威、季賢、幼賢、孝、達、季禮。

translations.literal: Seven sons: Bolian, Wei, Jixian, Youxian, Xiao, Da, and Jili.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Bolian, Wei, Jixian, Youxian, Xiao, Da, and Jili.

translations.literal: Wei was Magistrate of Yongshi and fathered Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei served as Magistrate of Yongshi and had a son Hong.

translations.literal: Three sons: Yao, Xie, and Zi, styled the Three Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had three sons: Yao, Xie, and Zi, known as the Three Ancestors.

translations.literal: The Tang clan had one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: One man of the Tang clan reached the chancellorship.

translations.literal: Xiujing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujing.
